a2-unit-42.42.1 At the pharmacy:
Narrator: Dialogue one.
Pharmacist: Next, please.
Woman: Hi. My son isn't feeling very well, and I want to get something to help. He feels pretty hot, and he has a dry cough.
Pharmacist: Have you taken his temperature?
Woman: No, I don't have a thermometer at home. How much do they cost?
Pharmacist: This one is twenty dollars. You should check his temperature regularly. If his fever goes very high or lasts for more than two days, you need to call the doctor.
Woman: OK. And for the cough?
Pharmacist: How old is he?
Woman: He's twelve.
Pharmacist: We have a very good cough syrup for kids. The instructions are on the side of the bottle. Has he ever had any side effects from cough medicine, like feeling sick or sleepy?
Woman: No, he hasn't.
Pharmacist: That's fine, then. Here you go.
Woman: Thanks. Where do I pay?
Pharmacist: Please pay my colleague at the register at the front.
Narrator: Dialogue two.
Pharmacist: Who's next?
Lucy: Hi! I'd like some advice about sunscreen and insect repellent. I'm going to an outdoor music festival next weekend. Last year I used some stuff from the supermarket, but it wasn't very good. What would you recommend?
Pharmacist: I recommend this sunscreen. Actually, all the sunscreens we sell give good protection, but you have to remember to put more on every couple of hours.
Lucy: OK, I'll take this one. And for mosquitoes? I got a lot of bites last year.
Pharmacist: We have a very good product, but it looks like there isn't any on the shelf right now. Let me just see if it's in stock. Ah, yes, here it is. It's more expensive than the supermarket stuff, but it really works.
Lucy: I'll give it a try. How much is that altogether?
Pharmacist: That's fifteen ninety-eight. Just tap your card on the machine. Thanks!
Narrator: Dialogue three.
Pharmacist: How can I help you?
Priya: I need this prescription filled, please.
Pharmacist: Sure. This is a refill for eye drops?
Priya: That's right. I have very dry eyes. I'm a medical student, so I study on my laptop a lot.
Pharmacist: So you already know that with this condition, it's important that you limit your time on the computer.
Priya: Yes, I know.
Pharmacist: And it's also a good idea to do some eye exercises every day.
Priya: Yes, my doctor explained. I'm doing them.
Pharmacist: Great. Here you go. Your insurance covers this, so you have nothing to pay. Just sign here.
Priya: Thanks so much!

Narrator: Number one. You can take it with food.
Narrator: Number two. You can't drive after you take this.
Narrator: Number three. You can't drink alcohol with this medicine.
Narrator: Number four. You can pay at the front.
Narrator: Number five. You can buy it without a prescription.
Narrator: Number six. You can't give this to children.
